comparator.name: Law
comparator.institution: Erasmus School of Law, Erasmus University Rotterdam
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 OER, Articles 10–11, confirms all 23 components and their credit weights: 60 EC in each year and 180 EC overall. The generic bachelor requires no named route. Article 13 allows a 15-EC minor from accessible EUR minors or an approved coherent external package. Articles 16–18 govern legal skills and the thesis. Article 43 and Appendix 5 require completion of B1 and 42 EC from B2 for entry to B3; the minor is accessible from the third enrolment year. Conditional access to JAV III and Recht en Bedrijf at 28 EC from B2 requires reaching 42 EC at the specified results checkpoints. Article 18 places research preparation in period 2 and the thesis in periods 3–4; the thesis accounts for 70% of the component grade, requires at least 6, and all parts must be completed. The ordinary full-time pathway reconstructed here completes each 60-EC year before progressing.
components: Introduction to International and European Union Law
15EC coherent minor chosen from accessible EUR minors; an external package requires Examination Board approval. This is constrained choice space.
Integrated legal and applied business-law component across periods 3 and 4.

10 EC of legal research preparation and bachelor-thesis work. Research preparation occurs in period 2, followed by the thesis in periods 3–4. The thesis accounts for 70% of the component grade, requires at least 6, and all parts must be completed.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Legal systems, rights, rules, responsibilities and legal argument
Law in social and economic context, including empirical study of law in action
Private, criminal, constitutional and administrative legal foundations
European Union and public international law and their relationship with national legal systems
Legal-academic research, writing, oral argument and an independent bachelor thesis
adjacent: Contracts, obligations, liability, property, insolvency and civil procedure
Substantive criminal law, criminal procedure and fair trial
Legal philosophy, ethics and theories of justice
Business law, commercial relationships and applied legal advice
questions: How can rights, rules and legal reasoning help resolve conflicts and social problems?
How do constitutional, administrative, European and international institutions organise and constrain public authority?
How does law structure private, commercial and organisational relationships?

trace: Mandatory Year1 personal and academic formation; not a substitute for legal-academic skills.
Complementary: reading financial statements supports analysis of the economic position of businesses and the commercial relationships studied in the law/business strand.
Complementary: AI bias, privacy, fairness, corporate governance and regulation provide a concrete contemporary application of commercial and social responsibility.
Direct: legal frameworks for cross-border contracts, trade, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce, applied through problem-based work and arbitration simulation.
Complementary: financial data, risk and investment/budget decisions explain the economic interests in commercial relationships; this is not a banking-law course.
Complementary: incentives, markets, firms and public intervention support the target’s explicit study of the social-economic function of law.
Complementary: strategic behaviour, imperfect competition, externalities and efficiency support analysis of how rules affect economic relationships; not competition-law doctrine.
Complementary: taxation, redistribution, externalities and public spending support analysis of public institutions and legal policy; not fiscal-law doctrine.
Complementary method: OLS, GLS and instrumental variables support empirical analysis of economic relationships, including the target’s law-in-action questions; not doctrinal legal research.
Complementary: cross-border governance, corporate responsibility and global trade analyse the institutional setting of international commercial relationships.

Complementary: experiential venture development exposes the commercial organisations and transactions examined in transnational business law and supplies its formal prerequisite; it does not teach law.
Complementary method: research design, sampling, experiments, surveys and statistics support empirical law-in-action inquiry; group research is not a law thesis.
Complementary skill: principled negotiation, objective criteria and simulations support conflict resolution and reasoned argument; not a legal procedure or moot-court course.
Direct: legal systems, sources and selected public/private fields are studied through legal, social and normative perspectives, case law and trial simulations.
Complementary: sovereignty, national self-determination, welfare states, decolonisation and European cooperation supply specific historical foundations for public authority.
Complementary: imperial power, theories of empire and great-power politics support the historical interpretation of international orders; not public international-law doctrine.
Direct: positive human-rights law, treaties, monitoring and case law are integrated with historical and philosophical arguments about rights.
Direct: accountability, guilt, legality, punishment, case analysis and a legal-aid simulation implement substantive criminal reasoning; no dedicated Dutch criminal-procedure sequence.
Direct: sources and subjects of international law, force, armed conflict, international crime, refugees, environmental law and treaty politics; coverage is not identical to the Erasmus syllabus.
Direct: comparative constitutional and administrative principles, government powers and civil liberties; not advanced Dutch administrative procedure.
Direct: comparative property, tort and contract principles in five legal systems; no dedicated Dutch obligations, insolvency or civil-procedure sequence.
Direct: EU institutions, legal foundations, fundamental rights, citizenship, free movement and domestic effects, using procedural work and substantive PBL cases.
Direct normative contribution: virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism support the target’s legal-philosophy themes; practical ethics is not a complete legal-philosophy syllabus.
Complementary: justification of political power and comparison of classical and contemporary political arguments support normative study of public authority.
Complementary: democratisation, state institutions, courts and the interaction of state and society support empirical analysis of constitutional government.
Complementary: competing international-relations theories and a Security Council simulation support analysis of the political operation of international orders.
Complementary: EU actors, decision rules and research on interest groups and legislative dossiers explain the political operation of EU law and public authority.
Complementary: theories of conflict, justice and reconciliation connect public authority, civil society and international institutional responses; not legal doctrine.
Complementary: social institutions, inequality and sociological theory support the target’s explicit law/society and empirical-law foundations.
Complementary method: qualitative design, data collection, interpretation and reflexivity support empirical investigation of law’s social operation.
Complementary: social-movement theory and environmental-justice cases explain how civic groups formulate justice claims and contest public decisions.
Complementary: civil society, public spheres, trust and empirical work with civic organisations support analysis of institutions and law’s social setting.
Complementary skill: rhetorical analysis, academic essays and oral arguments support reasoned communication; not legal drafting or doctrinal research.
Complementary skill: framing, persuasion ethics and applied institutional communication support public/legal argument; not the Erasmus legal moot court.

candidates.label: Public authority, European law and international institutions

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic law, legal-reasoning, law-and-society and criminal-law interests. Two further generator-backed directions remain especially coherent at UCR: public, international and European law; and private law, business and commercial relationships. Both are feasible and qualitatively distinct. The closest match and public route differ by six courses, the closest match and private/business route differ by eleven, and the two related routes differ by twelve. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore reached.

alternatives.label: Law, politics & society
alternatives.labelReason: Seven law/rights courses and one transnational business-law course supply substantial legal content alongside politics, society, economics and methods. This describes a related academic route, not Dutch professional legal training.
alternatives.concept: A programme connecting comparative legal reasoning in criminal, private, constitutional, international, EU and transnational business law with rights, justice, political institutions, social inquiry and economic analysis.
progression: The law gateway precedes all dependent law courses. Business Foundations in semester1 precedes the biennial Transnational Business Law course in semester4. Research Methods in semester2 precedes negotiation in semester4 and other dependent methods/economics study. Human rights follows the gateway and remains before advanced EU/constitutional study. All formal prerequisites and assigned offerings pass; no additional prerequisites are invented.

alternatives.label: Law, public institutions & international politics
alternatives.labelReason: Five law and rights courses support a programme whose larger curriculum studies public institutions, international politics, historical power, civil society, economics and empirical methods. The combined label reflects that balance.
alternatives.concept: A programme examining how public authority is established, justified and contested, combining constitutional, international and EU law and human rights with comparative and international politics, the history of states and empires, civil society, public economics and empirical inquiry.
alternatives.distinctness: Public authority and transnational orders organise this route. Compared with option1, it replaces criminal law, private law, transnational business law and the business prerequisite with modern history, empires, social movements and persuasive communication. These four substantive changes satisfy30EC in each direction; they support historical and civic inquiry rather than additional doctrinal law.
progression: The law gateway precedes constitutional, international and EU law. Foundations in comparative politics, sociology, political philosophy and modern history precede advanced EU politics, civil-society theory and negotiation. Qualitative methods may precede introductory sociology because its formal prerequisite is NONE and its research role is independently appropriate. Every assigned offering and formal prerequisite passes.

alternatives.label: Law, business & economic relationships
alternatives.labelReason: Eight legal and rights courses are combined with business, economics, finance, empirical methods and argumentation; the label does not imply a dedicated Dutch private-law degree.
alternatives.concept: A programme studying the legal and economic organisation of commercial relationships, combining comparative private, criminal, constitutional, international, EU and transnational business law with accounting, finance, corporate governance, empirical inquiry and ethical argument.
alternatives.distinctness: Commercial relationships organise this route. Accounting, finance, AI governance, international business, econometrics and rhetorical communication displace part of the closest option’s political and sociological sequence. Seven courses differ from option1 and ten from option2; this changes the inquiry from public institutions to legal/economic relationships.
progression: Law and business gateways precede dependent law and business courses. General research methods precedes econometrics and public economics; rhetoric precedes advanced persuasive communication. Qualitative inquiry complements economic analysis without replacing legal research. Every formal prerequisite and term offering passes.

blocks: Both introduce legal systems, sources, fields and the social operation of law; UCR does so comparatively rather than through a Dutch doctrinal sequence.
Partial correspondence in virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism and practical normative argument. UCR Ethics does not cover the comparator’s full legal-philosophy syllabus.
Both study public international law. UCR emphasises sources, conflict, refugees, environment and treaty politics; coverage is not identical.
Both examine constitutional and administrative institutions, public powers, legal limits and protected rights; UCR compares systems rather than teaching Dutch doctrine.
UCR has separate public-international-law and EU-law courses, but each is aligned to the comparator’s later dedicated component; it has no additional introductory combined course.
Comparative Constitutional Law already aligns to the comparator’s first-year combined state and administrative-law foundation; UCR has no second dedicated constitutional-law course.
Comparative Constitutional Law includes administrative-law foundations but UCR has no separate advanced Dutch administrative-law course.
Partial correspondence in comparative property, tort and contract principles. UCR does not teach the full Dutch private-law and procedural sequence.
Both introduce substantive criminal-law reasoning and criminal justice, including accountability and safeguards.
UCR Principles of Private Law includes contract and obligations but is already aligned to the introductory private-law component; there is no second dedicated obligations course.
UCR surveys property law but does not provide the comparator’s dedicated property-rights and insolvency sequence.
UCR has no dedicated course in Dutch civil procedure or enforcement.
UCR Criminal Law & Criminal Justice discusses procedure and safeguards but does not reproduce a dedicated Dutch criminal-procedure course.
UCR Criminal Law & Criminal Justice is already aligned to the introductory criminal-law component and does not form a second advanced Dutch-doctrine course.

Both apply legal reasoning to business relationships; UCR concentrates on transnational contracts, trade, investment and commercial disputes rather than the comparator’s integrated Dutch Law & Business project.
Complementary economic foundations, not equivalent legal analysis of the social costs and functions of legal rules.
UCR Public Economics analyses taxation economically but does not teach Dutch tax-law doctrine, sources, assessment or procedure.
Both support empirical study of institutions and social outcomes; UCR provides general research design and statistics rather than a law-specific empirical course.
Partial skills correspondence: rhetoric and academic argument, not the Dutch legal memo, procedural documents or dedicated legal-source training.
Partial skills correspondence: persuasion and institutional communication, not the required Dutch legal assignments and Moot Court.

The comparator requires advanced legal-academic skills and an independent bachelor thesis. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so the component remains unmatched and UCR’s optional independent-research element is displayed alongside it.

The comparator provides 15 EC of constrained minor choice: an accessible EUR minor or an approved coherent external package. UCR flexibility is distributed across its 180-EC programme, so no single scheduled course is its equivalent.

notes.text: These UCR programmes contain substantive comparative, European and international law, with different combinations of politics, society and business. Erasmus provides a much denser Dutch-law sequence, dedicated civil and criminal procedure, compulsory legal-academic skills and a bachelor thesis. UCR does not reproduce that jurisdiction-specific training or establish eligibility for regulated legal professions. The optional independent-research element is separate from the 24 scheduled courses and cannot supply the required legal thesis automatically.

audience.programmeDescription: Erasmus’s Law bachelor studies the Dutch legal system, private and criminal law, public authority, European and international law, and law’s economic and social setting. A three-year legal-skills sequence culminates in a bachelor thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related programmes combining substantive law with politics, society or business. They provide a broader academic study of legal and institutional questions, with less Dutch doctrine and procedure than Erasmus. They do not provide the same professional legal qualification route.

curriculum.limitation: The 15-EC minor is chosen from accessible EUR minors or an approved coherent external package. The ordinary full-time pathway completes 60 EC per year; entry to advanced study is subject to progression requirements.

componentNotes.y3-minor: 15 EC of constrained minor choice; external study requires approval.
componentNotes.y3-skills-thesis: 10 EC: research preparation and bachelor thesis. The thesis must receive at least 6 and accounts for 70% of this component’s grade.
